title: Operator compartmentalization: RBACv2 templates and pseudonymous audit ledger
author: Jordan Meyers
description: Context: enterprise customers and private deployments asked for better operator isolation and privacy-preserving audit trails. Motivation: reduce blast radius from operator credentials, make RBACv2 expressive enough to define compartment boundaries, and provide an auditable but pseudonymous ledger so security teams can investigate without exposing raw operator identifiers. This PR implements operator compartment templates for RBACv2, a pseudonymous audit ledger writer integrated with the audit pipeline, and optional KMS-scoped usage capping so tenant KMS calls are visible at compartment granularity. Changes include policy templates, policy-compiler hooks, a lightweight ledger writer service, a pseudonymization util (HMAC with per-region salt stored in KMS), unit + integration tests, and rollout tooling. Checklist: add RBAC templates and examples; hook policy-compiler to emit compartment claims; implement ledger writer and pseudonymizer; wire ledger into audit-forwarder with configurable retention; add KMS-scoped usage counters and config knobs; e2e test across hosted and private modes; document migration and rollback. Migration notes: old operator roles continue to function; we add companion migration job (tools/rbac/migrate_compartments) that annotates legacy bindings with compartment metadata. Rollout plan: staged canary on Dedicated, 48h monitoring window with audit fidelity checks, then enable private-installer blueprint. Backwards compatibility: none of the default behavior changes; new templates are opt-in. Related: references ENG-4528 for policy UX and SEC-211 for audit privacy requirements.

release_notes: Add RBACv2 operator compartment templates and a pseudonymous audit ledger. Opt-in templates for operator compartmentalization; privacy preserving audit ledger using KMS-backed per-region salts; optional KMS usage capping per compartment. No default behavioral changes; opt-in for private deployments. See docs/rbac/compartments.md and docs/operational/ledger-privacy.md for migration and operational guidance.
notes_for_sre: Watch ledger.write.latency and audit.forwarder.error_rate during canary. Verify KMS salt rotation logs and that pseudonymized IDs are stable across short rotation windows. If KMS errors spike, ledger falls back to hashed-shard id and emits SAFETY alert; rollback path: disable ledger forwarding via helm chart and re-route to legacy audit sink.
